raw_response:
I'm 70 this year, and I've been working this land since I was 20 — that's 50 years. I never went to school, can't read a word, but I know cotton like I know my own hands. It's just me and my old man at home now. Our son drives a truck in Shijiazhuang and our daughter married into a family two counties over. They send a little money at Spring Festival, but the rest of the year we're on our own.

All 8 mu is cotton. I tried wheat and maize once, 30 years ago, but the cotton pays better and I know how to grow it. I save my own seed every year — I pick the best bolls from the field before harvest and keep them in the dry corner of the house. But I always buy a little new seed from the shop to mix in, because saved seed gets weak after too many years. The shop man knows me, he gives me the same kind with the red picture on the bag. Costs about 25 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, I put down about one big bag of compound fertilizer for every two mu before planting. That's the white and blue bags — I don't know what's written on them, but the shop man says it's good for cotton. I spread it and work it in when we plow in April. Then when the cotton starts flowering in July, if the leaves look yellow, I topdress with urea — about half a small bag per mu, maybe 10 jin. Last year fertilizer got expensive and I thought I'd skip the topdress to save 300 yuan. Big mistake. The bolls were small and I lost more than I saved. Never doing that again.

I irrigate twice. Once right after planting in late April if the soil is dry, and once when the bolls are forming in July. The well is there, but pumping costs electricity money — about 30 yuan each time for 8 mu. I can't afford to water more than that. When I was younger I carried water by hand, but my back can't do that now.

Cotton needs spraying. The bollworm comes every year like clockwork, and the weeds grow fast in summer. I spray four times total — twice for weeds, twice for worms. I buy the cheap bottles from the village supply store. Auntie Li down the road buys the expensive stuff, but she has 15 mu and her son helps her. I use what I can afford.

For labor, me and my husband do the planting, weeding, and spraying. But picking — that's the hard part. 8 mu of cotton is too much for two old people. The bolls open in September and you have to pick them before they get wet or dirty. We hire four or five women from the village for about 8 days total. They want 80 yuan a day now, plus I feed them lunch. It hurts to pay that, but without them the cotton rots in the field. Last year we tried to do more ourselves and my husband's knees swelled up for a week.

I expect about 260 jin per mu this year if the weather is decent. Last year was dry and we only got 220. I'm not changing anything — at 70, I know what works. I need enough from this crop to buy our blood pressure medicine and keep rice on the table. Total costs this year are about 3,200 yuan. That's a lot for us, but skimping costs more in the end.
